newsitem.title: USA: S. Dakota wheat plantings near five-year average.
newsitem.headline: S. Dakota wheat plantings near five-year average.

text.p: South Dakota spring wheat plantings neared the five-year average despite the slow start as warmer, dry weather allowed for fieldwork, the State Agricultural Statistics Service said.

Spring wheat was 76 percent seeded as of Sunday, trailing the five-year average of 82 percent but well ahead of the previous week's pace of 48 percent. The crop was rated six percent poor, 38 fair, 50 good and six percent excellent.
Corn was 59 percent seeded, against the five-year average of 49 percent. Soybean plantings were 14 percent complete, versus 19 percent average.
Winter wheat was rated nine percent very poor, 23 percent poor, 31 fair, 33 percent good and four percent excellent.

"There are some reports of farmers tearing up winter wheat and reseeding to another crop," the report said. "Due to the late planting season, some farmers are electing not to plant any more spring wheat and are switching to a later crop, such as corn."
Range and pasture were rated one percent very poor, nine percent poor, 35 fair, 48 good and seven percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent very poor, five percent short, 74 percent adequate and 20 percent surplus.
